newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq condemns Turkey over incursion.
newsitem.headline: Iraq condemns Turkey over incursion.

text.p: An official Iraqi newspaper condemned Turkey on Thursday for sending troops into northern Iraq in pursuit of separatist Kurdish rebels.
"Such an operation is condemned and rejected," said al-Thawra newsapaper, organ of the ruling Baath party.

Turkish troops, backed by air support, crossed into northern Iraq on Monday pursuing rebels of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), the Anatolian news agency said, quoting a statement from Turkey's armed forces. The statement did not say how many troops crossed into Iraq but it said at least 43 rebels were killed.
The PKK uses bases in northern Iraq outside Baghdad's control as part of its guerrilla war for self-rule in southeast Turkey. Turkish troops have crossed into Iraq several times in large numbers.

The Iraqi newspaper also condemned U.S. air patrols over northern Iraq which are meant to protect Kurds against possible attacks by Baghdad. Al-Thawra said the Turkish incursion into northern Iraq "exposes U.S. lies that the so-called 'aerial surveillance force' aims at safeguarding the Kurds."
"As usual the (U.S-led) force has done nothing toward the military operations by Turkish troops against Iraqi Kurdish villages near the border with Turkey," the paper said.
Last week Turkey allowed the United States and Britain to continue using its airbases to mount patrols over northern Iraq. France withdrew from the operation, earning Iraq's praise.
